comment: No source is published; the maker's README is at github.com/phestrada/OME. Two faults are worth knowing. First, a second ParamWidget for the Tempo CV trimmer is built at the very end of the widget's constructor and given the position of the end-of-cycle output jack, so the panel carries two widgets for parameter 4 and the eoc jack has a knob drawn on top of it; the library screenshot shows the knob there. The help click still resolves to the jack, because the port's box is the smaller of the two, but a mouse drag reaches the knob first. Second, every one of the eight CV inputs MULTIPLIES its knob by the incoming voltage rather than adding to it, so a patched cable sitting at 0V drives the parameter to its clamp floor. The root and octave CVs carry one further special case: when their knob is at zero the jack sets the value on its own. Two parameter tooltips are stale — parameter 11 is the pattern trimmer but is named Division CV, and parameter 19 is the steps trimmer but is named Size CV. Inputs 7 and 9 were never passed to configInput, so they hover with no name; they are the octave and chord CV inputs. Parameters 1, 2 and 3 were never passed to configParam either, so the clock, run and reset buttons hover with no name, but Module::config gives them a working 0-to-1 quantity, so they do work. The README calls the control under the clock jack a light; the code reads it as a manual step button. The internal clock is an exponential of the tempo parameter, 60 BPM at the default, and it is used only when nothing is patched to the clock input.
